programs.title: Passion - a way of life
programs.desc: The program shows the lives of extraordinary people who infect others with their inventiveness and courage.The protagonists of the documentary are both people involved in sports and people who found their vocation in unusual interests, including:designing and building miniatures or taking photos from the air.Viewers will learn, among others:Andrzej Bargiel, who became famous for skiing from the eight-thousander Broad Peak.Another hero of the program will be Sebastian Kawa, a glider pilot who has already won 15 gold medals in the World and European Championships.

programs.title: It's beautiful here
programs.desc: Dorota Szelągowska will visit unique places in Poland, the existence of which only insiders often know.The host will prove that it is never too late to fulfill your childhood dream and live in a tree house, at least for a while.For those who value greater comfort, he will show luxurious interiors created, among others, by:in an old cotton fabric factory.Viewers will also meet the owners of these charming places, who will tell their stories and reveal how they managed to implement their unique plans and projects.Many of them abandoned life in big cities to be able to do what they love most, i.e. interior design and running unique guesthouses.Dorota Szelągowska will look into every nook and cranny of these original buildings, reveal interior design ideas to viewers and prove that there are many wonderful places in Poland that are truly beautiful.

programs.title: Taste the world with Pascal
programs.desc:
Pascal Brodnicki likes to explore the world through his sense of taste.He loves to prepare various dishes at street stalls, in African villages or on the beach. However, during his culinary journeys it was not always easy for him.Sometimes elephants stole his ingredients.Of course, Pascal couldn't deny himself the pleasure of tasting local delicacies.In Delhi, he stopped for a long time at a paratha stand, in a Zanzibar village he ate rice with coconut, and in Namibia he tried a zebra steak."Taste the world with Pascal" is not only about cooking.The host visited an elephant orphanage in Sri Lanka, fed cheetahs in Africa and climbed a coconut tree.In Bombay he became a teacher and taught Polish to children, and on the coast of Zanzibar he hunted octopus.Everywhere his passion and positive energy attracted crowds of onlookers
This time Pascal went to Namibia, famous for its cow breeding and delicious beef.The chef grills his favorite steaks here and, as usual, he will do it in an unusual place.This time on the farm where they are kept.tamed cheetahs.After meeting the big cats, Pascal sets off north of the country, to Opuwo, where he goes to a supermarket.Here he meets half-naked women from the Himba tribe who are shopping.He also visits the market where he buys a gift for the Herrero tribe - a goat.His gesture wins great acclaim and Pascal is welcomed into the village with an amazing dance.

The next stop on the "Taste the World with Pascal" map is India.Pascal will visit Delhi, where he will taste parathas, traditional wheat pancakes, served with green peas, carrots, bananas or cheese at street stalls.At one of the stalls, Pascal will serve passers-by chicken "Indian style" according to his own recipe.The leader will also visit temples where volunteers prepare free meals for pilgrims.In such kitchens, people cook for up to a thousand people.The cook had never cooked on such a scale.Later, Pascal will go to Bombay, where he will look for the perfect fish for his recipe at the fish market.And then he will prepare it in curry sauce, with peppers and coconut milk.A saleswoman at the local market lends him the kitchen.

The next stage of the African journey is Zanzibar, a beautiful and multicultural island in the Indian Ocean.The local cuisine is a mix of many flavors from around the world.Pascal will go to the Forodhani market, famous for its delicious skewers with colorful stalls.He will discover the secrets of the plantain, also called "elephant's trunk", i.e. a sweet banana, which on the island is treated not as a fruit, but as a vegetable.Pascal will go octopus fishing.Zanzibar is also known for its colorful reefs, white sand, schools of rainbow fish and beautiful coastline.Pascal will set up his kitchen on one of such paradise beaches.This time, he will use a piece of a wooden boat as a countertop, and a natural rock depression filled with sea water as a sink.The chef will use local specialties and prepare seafood in spice sauce.He will invite a group of local women to his feast, who will return the favor with a dinner in a nearby village.
